title: Audit CRT reservoir placement and split-axis coordinate descriptors
body:
PR4100's CRT switch controls can read an entire left child. Its borrowed-field placement therefore needs more than avoidance of the target axes: it must preserve those dense dependencies after coordinate exchanges. This adds a constructive audit of CRT.md §3, including the root's inactive-quarter choice and axes split by placement.

The quantified proof covers the original mixed-width domain and constants. It gives at most 25,600 batches per synchronized switch layer, three mutually disjoint field exchanges plus their inverses, and at most d+12 coordinate fragments. Full dirty-state restoration is conditional on the completed repaired switch's all-address contract. The allocator and verifier make the coordinates and counterexamples independently inspectable.

Validation on Python 3.12.13:
- Registered ordinary and optimized replay passed: 104,864 production descriptor plans / 524,288 active-axis visits; all 4,096 dirty addresses of a separate reduced root-axis caller; 28,672 layer conjugations; 86,016 omission checks; forward/inverse composition; six semantic controls.
- Package metadata and pins, committed-byte/source-history preflight, and deterministic export integrity passed.
- Git-free optimized export replay reproduced the receipt without changing exported bytes; modified predecessor source bytes were rejected.

The large run is a descriptor census. The finite caller is a root-axis projection using ideal completed-switch endpoints, not a raw compact-macro replay. No complete control evaluator, ordinary-callee implementation, last-K tail, sorting tariff, numerical claim, full CRT/multiplication theorem, or new κ is asserted. The selected frontier is unchanged.

Starts independently from canonical main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244` under priority revision 7. PR4169's repair result is complementary context, not an executable dependency. Canonical coordination: [Discussion #4173](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4173). Open next question: bind split-axis descriptors to the actual fixed-tape E(p,ell) evaluator and account for scans, exchanges, erasure and head returns.

Credit: Cinna Davis's PR4100 supplies the audited construction; Vlado Vojdanovski's PR1673 and Jose Manuel's physical support router supply the predecessor exchange/recoloring methods. Retained compact/routing lineage is credited in the package. Prepared by Hiroki KUMAZAKI (@kumagi) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; new work Apache-2.0. This is not independent human review or formal proof-assistant verification.
